findings.value: A Grade II-listed 1930s art deco building that opened as a cinema in 1933, was later used as an opera school and bingo hall, and now hosts concerts, club nights and other events.

evidence.quote: This characterful Grade II-listed building opened in 1933 as one of London's biggest and flashiest cinemas.
It spent time as an opera school and a bingo hall
blending the venue’s 1930s Art Deco heritage with modern, audience-first design

findings.value: Live concerts, club nights, MMA fights and immersive cinema.

evidence.quote: including MMA fights, immersive cinema, club nights and a huge range of live music concerts

findings.value: The venue says it built a reputation for LGBTQ+-led events in 2019.

evidence.quote: In 2019 Troxy cemented its reputation as one of the flagship venues for LGBTQ+ led events.

notes: The Time Out page (dated 2023-03-10) still carries a 'Temporarily closed' tag in its keywords. Troxy's own history page, read today, describes events in 2024 and 2025 and a 2026 capacity rise to 3,600, so the venue is open and no closing news was found; this tag is stale. Two WebSearches were not used on it (budget kept). The accessibility and FAQ pages were not re-read this run, so the existing profile's quotes from them are unchanged.
